subject: chemistry
title: Human activity and climate change: the evidence
key_idea: Human activities add carbon dioxide and methane to the atmosphere. Many scientists believe this will raise the Earth's temperature and cause climate change. Evidence must be evaluated for quality, uncertainty and peer review.

sections.heading: Human activities that add greenhouse gases

blocks.text: This section covers the activities that increase carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere.

items.meaning: An increase in the mean temperature of the atmosphere at the Earth's surface.
A long-term change in weather patterns across the Earth.
Clearing forests, which means less photosynthesis to take in carbon dioxide.

items: Burning **fossil fuels** for energy, electricity and transport.
**Deforestation** to make farmland, housing or space for industry.
Farming livestock such as cattle, and growing rice in paddy fields.
Waste in landfill, which produces methane as it decomposes.
Fossil fuel use and the destruction of peat bogs.
Reduce livestock farming and the number of rice (paddy) fields.
Reduce the amount of rubbish going to landfill.
Use methane from landfill as an energy source.
Reduce fossil fuel use and the destruction of peat bogs.

diagram.alt: Sort human activities by the greenhouse gas they add to the atmosphere.
diagram.prompt: Sort each activity by the main greenhouse gas it adds.

items: Fossil fuel burning and deforestation add carbon dioxide.
Livestock, rice fields and landfill add methane.

blocks.text: This section covers why a growing population links to more greenhouse gases.

items: More people need more energy and transport, so more fossil fuels are burned.
More people need more farmland, so more forests are cleared.
More people need more food, so more cattle are kept and more rice is grown.
More people produce more waste, which produces methane as it decomposes.
Link population to what people need, then to the gas that results.
Energy and farmland link to carbon dioxide. Food and waste link to methane.

blocks.text: This section covers how to judge evidence about climate change.

items.meaning: A link between two sets of data, such as carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.
Checking of a scientist's results by other scientists before they are accepted.

items: Evidence compares the change in atmospheric carbon dioxide, fossil fuel use and temperature.
Many scientists believe human activities will cause the Earth's temperature to rise, based on peer-reviewed evidence.
It is difficult to model such a complex system, so models are simplified.
Opinions in the media may be based on only part of the evidence and may be biased.
Possible effects of global warming include melting ice and rising sea levels.
Where measurements are taken, because data from one city or country is not a global figure.
How accurate historical measurements are.
A time lag between emissions and their effect.
Emissions from other sources may also matter.
Data about emissions alone does not show a change in temperature.

blocks.text: Practise calculating an increase in carbon dioxide concentration, in parts per million (ppm).

diagram.alt: Calculate the increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration between two dates.
diagram.question: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere was {a} ppm in an earlier year and {b} ppm in a later year. Calculate the increase in ppm, to the nearest whole number.
working: Increase = {answer} ppm to the nearest whole number

items: Evaluate evidence by its quality, its uncertainties and whether it was peer reviewed.
A correlation is a link. Check where and how the data was collected.

checks.q: Give two human activities that increase the amount of methane in the atmosphere.
checks.a: Any two from: keeping livestock such as cattle, growing rice in paddy fields, waste decomposing in landfill.

checks.q: Explain why an increase in the world population may increase the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
checks.a: More energy is needed, so more fossil fuels are burned. Or more farmland is needed, so there is more deforestation.

checks.q: Give one reason why data about carbon dioxide emissions from one country may not show the effect on global temperature.
checks.a: The data is not a global figure, or there is a time lag between emissions and their effect, or emissions from other sources also matter.

worked_example.question:
In the past 50 years, there has been an increase in:
• the world population
• the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere
• the concentration of methane in the atmosphere
• the mean temperature of the atmosphere at the Earth's surface.

Most scientists think this information can be used to explain climate change.

Explain why the increase in world population may have caused the increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
answer_points: More energy (or transport) is required, so more fossil fuels are burned.
OR more farmland is required, so there is more deforestation.
worked_example.tip: Both marks are linked: the need, then the activity. A named fossil fuel is allowed.

worked_example.question:
Many people are concerned by the increasing amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

The amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is measured in parts per million (ppm).

The amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere in June 2001 and in June 2021 was:

June 2001: 371.17 ppm
June 2021: 416.56 ppm

Calculate the increase in the amount of carbon dioxide, in ppm, from June 2001 to June 2021.

Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
worked_example.tip: 45 on its own scores both marks. One mark is for correct rounding of the difference of the two numbers.

items: Consider the correlation between change in carbon dioxide concentration, fossil fuel consumption and temperature change.
Consider the uncertainties caused by where measurements are taken.
Consider the uncertainties caused by the accuracy of historical measurements.

worked_example.question:
In the last 75 years there has been an increase in both:

• the world population
• the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

Why may the increase in the world population have caused the increase in the concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?
answer_points: More energy is required, so more fossil fuels are burned.
OR more farmland, or land for housing and industry, is required, so there is more deforestation.
worked_example.tip: More electricity, transport or manufacturing is allowed for more energy. Answers in terms of respiration are ignored.
